title: Prescription-delay respondents show distinct same-round health and employment surfaces
source_unit: MEPS 2024 HC-256 person record with valid prescription-delay field and same-round perceived-health/employment outcomes

denominator.unit: valid HC-256 person records for both displayed outcomes

poor_or_fair_health.unit: percent; standard BRR SE 1.9563; approximate 95% CI 28.0087–35.6774

employed_at_round_5_or_3.unit: percent; standard BRR SE 2.1564; approximate 95% CI 50.8334–59.2866

observations.method: Same-round descriptive comparison using PERWT24F and 128 BRR replicate flags.
observations.uncertainty: The delay field and outcomes are same-round and may reflect illness severity, coverage, access, prior employment, and reporting; this is not a post-delay outcome estimate.
observations.subgroup: MEPS 2024 respondents reporting prescription delay with valid perceived-health and employment fields.
observations.counterinterpretation: Prescription delay may be a marker of underlying need or access complexity rather than the cause of health or employment status.

denominator.unit: valid HC-256 person records for both displayed outcomes

poor_or_fair_health.unit: percent; standard BRR SE 0.3210; approximate 95% CI 9.3919–10.6503

employed_at_round_5_or_3.unit: percent; standard BRR SE 0.5052; approximate 95% CI 48.3300–50.3105

observations.method: Same-round descriptive comparison using PERWT24F and 128 BRR replicate flags.
observations.uncertainty: No-delay is not a randomized comparison or proof of medication access; the outcome fields do not establish timing after a prescription episode.
observations.subgroup: MEPS 2024 respondents not reporting prescription delay with valid perceived-health and employment fields.
observations.counterinterpretation: Different health need, age, insurance, employment, and reporting composition can generate the contrast without a delay effect.

related_sources.claim: Reader-facing same-round prescription-delay health/work comparison and limits.
Machine output preserves the 19,140-record input, field-specific valid counts, estimates, and BRR uncertainty.
Longitudinal prescription-delay direction record is a separate round-to-round design.

reproduction_audit.result: The two same-round subgroup observations reproduce the committed local output; raw archives remain outside the repository.
reproduction_audit.interpretation: This record strengthens the exposure/context screen, not a causal prescription-delay, recovery, trust, political-action, or household-burden estimate.

boundary: This is a same-round MEPS comparison. Prescription delay, perceived health, and employment are not linked as a dated medication episode; person weights are not household weights. No causal effect, treatment continuity, recovery, remedy, trust, political action, or exit claim is made.
